The text provided exhibits significant bias through the use of subjective and pejorative language. Describing the movie as "nothing more than a mindless spectacle" and "lowbrow entertainment" reflects a personal value judgment rather than an objective critique. Furthermore, the argument employs an appeal to elitism by suggesting that only "discerning viewers" can see the truth, implying that the general audience is uncritical or easily manipulated. This framing creates an "us versus them" dynamic, dismissing the film's success as merely appealing to the masses while positioning the critic as superior. The argumentation relies on these loaded terms to invalidate the movie's artistic merit without providing specific, objective evidence of its flaws.
